sec: ADPKD: cyst infection treatment & ESRD/nephrectomy · p788

items.q: The antibiotics that penetrate cysts in ADPKD are remembered as CCC, namely:
items.exp: Antibiotics that penetrate cysts (CCC): ciprofloxacin, cotrimoxazole and carbapenems — used for cyst infection. (Book p788)

items.q: A patient with ADPKD and cyst infection requires antibiotics. Which set is appropriate?
items.exp: Cyst-penetrating antibiotics in ADPKD are ciprofloxacin, cotrimoxazole and carbapenems (CCC). (Book p788)

items.q: In ADPKD, renal transplantation reverses the extrarenal associations such as liver cysts.
opts: False — extrarenal associations cannot be reversed
True — transplantation cures the liver cysts
True, but only for colonic diverticula
False — renal transplantation is contraindicated in ADPKD
items.exp: For ESRD (CKD) in ADPKD renal transplant is done, but extrarenal associations cannot be reversed — liver cysts, colonic diverticulum, saccular aneurysm, mitral valve prolapse, aortic root dilatation and hernias persist. (Book p788)

items.q: Match the extrarenal association of ADPKD with the description given — 1) Liver cysts  2) Colonic diverticulum  3) Saccular aneurysm of anterior circulation … A) A listed extrarenal association  B) The commonest extrarenal association  C) Significant if >10 mm
items.exp: Extrarenal associations of ADPKD: liver cysts (m/c); colonic diverticulum; saccular aneurysm of the anterior circulation (>10 mm is significant); mitral valve prolapse; AR/aortic root dilatation; abdominal wall/inguinal hernia. (Book p788)

items.q: A saccular aneurysm of the anterior circulation in ADPKD is considered significant when it exceeds:
items.exp: Saccular aneurysm of anterior circulation in ADPKD: >10 mm is significant. (Book p788)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as an extrarenal association of ADPKD?
items.exp: Congenital hepatic fibrosis/Caroli's syndrome belongs to ARPKD (biliary duct involvement); ADPKD has liver cysts, colonic diverticulum, saccular aneurysm, mitral valve prolapse, aortic root dilatation and hernias. (Book p788)
